Free registration and a demo account.
cons: No independent audit of the models.
Broker relationship described vaguely.
Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
redFlags: Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.

faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
The final score lands at 4.7 - a capable platform held back by its own paperwork. Start small, verify the claims yourself and never trade money you cannot lose.
